main_text.l: authoritate & observare & instituere, quæ nullibi
constat fuisse vel ab ipso Deo, vel à Mose Dei mi-
nistro præcepta. Accipite instantias è multis pau-
cas. Primò, Paschatis Solennitatem ex Lege
Mosis septiduo observandam, Speciali Lege Rex Hezekias
(qui tamen singulare pietatis suæ testimonium
à Deo ipso accipere meruit) ex populi consensu in
alterum septiduum continuari decrevit. Cujus
rei historia extat, 2 Paralip. 30. Secundò, festum Pu-
rim in memoriam ejus liberationis, quæ Judæorum
genti sub Persarum Rege Assuero contigerat, an-
nuatim celebrari instituerunt Ester & Mardochæi,
Esth. 9. Tertiò, cùm Moses diem solennis jejunii an-
nuatim unicum duntaxat, Septimo mense, observan-
dum præcepisset; Reges & Magistratus illius po-
puli (quibus de causis non satis constat, sed ut par
est credere, in memoriam insignium aliquot judi-
ciorum Dei) annua solemnia jejunia authoritate suâ
instituerunt alia: ita ut temporibus ultimorum
prophetarum quatuor observarentur annua jejunia:
videlicet, præter illum Septimi mensis, tria alia;
mensibus quarto, quinto & decimo; quorum omn-
ium fit mentio, Zachar. 8. 19. Quartò, festum
dedicationis Altarii, quod Encænia dicitur ab
Assamoni[?] sine aliquo Dei mandato institutum, (cujus histo-
ria ex 1 Macc. 4. 59. petenda est,) Christus ipse
non tantum comprobasse, sed & præsentiâ suâ co-
honestasse, plurimorum eorúmque melioris notæ
interpretum judicio exîstimatur, Joh. 10. 22. Quin-
tò, ut in solennibus jejuniis & luctu pœnitentiali
sacro se induerent, & cineres crinibus inspergerent,
nullo Dei mandato præceptum legimus; apud Ju-
dæos tamen, longò per aliquot retrò secula usu ita
moribus receptum est (consuetudine diuturnâ, ut
fieri amat, vim legis obtinente,) ut Christus eo lo-
quendi genere, tanquam ex recepto more gentis,
sine aliquo affixo nigro Theta, aliquoties usus fuerit:

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The margin numbers 1 to 5 stand beside the lines where the paragraph-numbers are printed; they are placed as notes at those lines. "Assamoni" is the least certain reading (marked [?]); the scan is blurred there. The word "Theta" is printed in Latin letters in italics and is copied as printed. Show-through and the neighbouring page's edge at the right are left out. The text runs over the whole page as one paragraph, because no line is indented and none ends short of the margin before the last line. The final line is the last full line; "ut" is the catchword.
